main.content:
Turtle-WoW implements cross-faction features, allowing horde and alliance to join parties together, do dungeons and raids, mail, trade in a party, and every Auction House in the game is also merged into one, so horde and alliance can easily trade for a single server economy.

NPC reputations are still in place, so alliance players are still permanently hated by horde NPCs and vice versa, so while xfaction party summoning does does open up alliance RFC and horde Stockades, the guards might cause trouble. Because many quests still remain faction exclusive, there are plenty of quest and reputation reward items that remain exclusive for their faction. The NPC rep issues also mean that players wishing to play together xfaction, will have a good time mob grinding, but as for xfaction questing, they will be mostly restricted to neutral faction quests (which are sharable xfaction), and the few later leveling quests that have both horde and alliance versions for the same quest objectives.

PVP is also not cross faction; battlegrounds remain horde vs alliance. As for world PVP in xfaction parties, PVP within them is fine, however faction A healing and assisting a faction B player is prohibited by the server rules.

In PVE group dungeoning and raiding, Paladins' and Shamans' totems blessings and auras now all stack with eachother—however, Magic Resist auras do not stack with eachother nor Mark of the Wild, only the strongest will take effect.

A hidden grove in southern Ashenvale overlooking Mystral Lake that was once a retreat for druids for several years, an evil presence has taken root in the region. ==History== Originally a hidden grove that served as a calm retreat for druids, in recent times the Groveweald tribe has moved in while fleeing the madness of the Foulweald tribe, expelling several of the original inhabitants in the process. However, in spite of their attempts to escape the madness, they succumbed to it in time. Kalanar Brightshine once lived here, before he was expelled from the Grove by the Groveweald furbolgs and his home was burned down. Demonic forces of the Burning Legion led by the doomguard Master Raxxieth have established themselves within the grove, beginning to corrupt the glade. '''Corthan''' (or the '''Kingdom of Corthan'''<ref>{{questlong|Neutral|37|A King's Plea}}</ref>) was an ancient kingdom of [[Azotha]]<ref name=":0">[https://discord.com/channels/466622455805378571/528228771594240030/1274061839482753157 Moriena from the Turtle WoW Community Discord] (dead link) - "Corthan was a kingdom of the Azotha"</ref><ref name=":1">[[The History of Corthan]]</ref> situated in the present-day region of the [[Badlands]]. They were a warlike people<ref name=":1" /> who conquered and subjugated the lesser tribes of the area. Corthan's ruler was called the Marauder King; those who took up this mantle were also thereafter called Corthan.<ref>[https://discord.com/channels/466622455805378571/528228771594240030/1086438286467272736 Gheor from the Turtle WoW Community Discord] (dead link) - "It is basically implied that all high priests and their children are named after Zeth. The FK's name is Zeth, and his daughters name is Zetharia. At one point in time the duty of High Priest was given to his daugther - they abandon their old names when they get these titles -, same as Corthan."</ref>

Corthan maintained an ironclad grip on the region through continuous warfare. Despite their ferocity and skill in combat, the fallout of a love feud between the last Marauder King and the Keeper of of Zeth's daughter, [[Zetharia]], ultimately spelled the doom of the nation, when the latter called forth the dark forces of the [[God of Everlasting Death|Lord of Everlasting Death]], who ensnared Corthan's inhabitants in a curse of undeath forever.

== History ==
Corthan was formed from a group of Azotha.<ref name=":0" /> Its birth predates the rise of [[Arathi Empire|Arathor]]; it is suggested that the Arathi dynasty may have been established by rebels who fled north from Corthan.<ref>[https://discord.com/channels/466622455805378571/528228771594240030/1086439363199635568 Gheor from the Turtle WoW Community Discord] (dead link) - "The Kingdom of Corthan predates the Arathor Empire. Corthan mentions rebels going up north of the now Badlands and implies they have gone back into a tribal state - thus being the first step towards the Empire of Arathor."</ref> 

The land of Corthan was ruled by many kings, who each had the strength to vie for, and dominate, the region, with "a fist of iron, and strength eternal."  Corthan would go on to weather many storms, including drought, disease, and famine. The nation also warred with its neighbors constantly to maintain its dominion over the land; this penchant for warfare, however, would end up weakening the principles of its people over time.<ref name=":1" />

Corthan was still conquering neighboring tribes by the time of the last [[Marauder King Corthan]], who solidified his rule by offering amnesty to the defeated chieftains and warlords of the area in exchange for their loyalty.<ref>Events of {{questlong|Neutral|37|The Land of Kings}}.</ref> Corthan would later enter a betrothal to Zetharia, the daughter of the Keeper of Zeth, who resided in the [[Ruins of Zeth|High Temple of Zeth]]. While Zetharia doted upon the Marauder King, the arrangement soon fell apart when Corthan brought his commoner mistress with him on the day of his wedding ceremony.<ref name=":2">Events of {{questlong|Neutral|37|The Curse of Zetharia}}.</ref> 

Heartbroken and enraged by Corthan's unrequited love, Zetharia confined herself to her bedroom for days, where she consulted many tomes. On the day of Corthan's marriage to his commoner sweetheart, Zetharia emerged from her room. Having made a necromantic pact with the Lord of Everlasting Death, Zetharia cursed the Marauder King, his new wife, and his very kingdom to suffer an eternity of undeath, for all time. 

The kingdom once possessed a powerful Azotha artifact called the [[Hand of Corthan]]. Long after Corthan's fall, [[Dark Bishop Mordren]] sent Horde adventurers to retrieve the ancient artifact.<ref>{{questlong|Horde|40|For the Collection}}</ref>

== People and culture ==

=== Religion ===
Zeth appears to have been the religion of Corthan. All high priests and their children are named after Zeth (similarly to the naming tradition of each Marauder King being called Corthan).<ref name=":2" /> While the specifics are unknown, the worship centers around an entity called the "Lord of the Living Flame." The [[Ruins of Zeth]] was once the high temple of Zeth, and it is there where the flame of kings is located, under the care of the Keeper.

== Speculation ==
* One of the runes in the Molten Core is called the Rune of Zeth; it is possible that the Lord of Everlasting Flame is Ragnaros.

The '''Council of Six''',<ref>[[Khadgar's Journal]]</ref><ref name="Modera daughter">[[Magistrate Modera#Quotes]]</ref> also known as the '''Six''',<ref>[[Archmage Angela Dosantos#Quotes]]</ref> is the name given to the [[Kirin Tor]] high council of [[Dalaran (kingdom)|Dalaran]]. These six individuals were the leaders of both the city and all territories under the control of Dalaran. The Six were usually the most senior, but not necessarily the most gifted. They were chosen by several means, magic but one of them.<ref name="DotD1">''[[Day of the Dragon]]'', chapter 1</ref>

Traditionally, the membership of the Council of Six was kept a strict secret. When someone met with the Council officially, it was always in a special, enchanted chamber, the Chamber of the Air, a room with no visible walls — the gray stone floor with its central diamond symbol stood beneath an open sky that shifted and changed rapidly, as if the time sped past within the chamber.<ref name="DotD1" />

==Known members==
===Current===
* [[Modera]] - Member after the Second War<ref>''[[Day of the Dragon]]'', chapter 13</ref> and in the years leading up to the Third War.<ref name="RtD" /> Still a member to this day, working on the reconstruction of Dalaran.<ref name="Modera daughter" />

===Former===
* [[Kael'thas Sunstrider]] - Prince of Quel'Thalas, member in the years leading up to the Third War.<ref name="RtD">''[[Road to Damnation]]''</ref> Departed from the Alliance after the Third War and joined the [[Illidari]].
* [[Kel'Thuzad]] - Expelled for practicing necromancy, then traveled to Northrend and formed the Cult of the Damned to serve the Lich King.<ref name="RtD" />
* [[Krasus]] - Humanoid form of [[Korialstrasz]]. Member after the Second War,<ref>''[[Day of the Dragon]]'', chapter 2</ref> but took his leave from the Council several years before the Third War to be with [[Alexstrasza]].<ref>''[[Day of the Dragon]]'', chapter 21</ref>
* [[Antonidas]] - Head of the Kirin Tor during the [[Third War]].<ref>''Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos'' Game Manual, ''[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_III:_Reign_of_Chaos_Game_Manual#Antonidas Heroes and Villains]'', Antonidas</ref> Killed by [[Arthas Menethil]].
* [[Drenden]] - Member after the Second War<ref>''[[Day of the Dragon]]'', chapter 12</ref> and in the years leading up to the Third War.<ref name="RtD" /> Unknown status after the Third War.

[[Image:Corin's Crossing.jpg|thumb|Corin's Crossing]]
[[Corin's Crossing]] used to be a fairly prosperous crossroads trading town.  Surrounded by the farmlands of [[Lordaeron]] and located strategically at a crossroads connecting [[Andorhal]], [[Stratholme]], and [[Tyr's Hand]], Corin's Crossing was a common stop for traders and travelers.  After the [[Scourge]] turned the breadbasket of Lordaeron into the toxic [[Plaguelands]], Corin's Crossing has become an outpost of the Scourge.  Travelers are advised to give the town a wide berth, as it is crawling with minions of the Scourge (levels 55+).  Even rogues using stealth are advised not to attempt to sneak through the town as there are dark shades present that can detect invisible units.

[[image:CryptFiend.png|thumb|A crypt fiend]]
The cunning crypt fiends were once the lords of the ancient spider kingdom of [[Azjol-Nerub]] that ruled over the arctic land of [[Northrend]] in ancient times. However, the [[Lich King]] destroyed the [[Nerubian]] civilization and took control of the frozen continent. The Nerubians that had fallen in the war were resurrected as slaves for the Lich King's army. These reanimated insectoids became known as the crypt fiends because they still wear the tattered remains of the linens in which their corpses were mummified. These aberrant creatures are capable of summoning swarms of vile insects and projecting web-like strands to incapacitate and harm their enemies.

Crypt Fiends can be found the [[Eastern Plaguelands]], [[Stratholme]] and [[Scholomance]]  There is also a Crypt Fiend in [[Razorfen Downs]], and another one that somehow ended up in [[Blackrock Depths]].

[[Image:cryptlord.jpg|thumb|A nerubian Crypt Lord]]
These ancient, evil behemoths were once the mighty kings of the subterranean spider kingdom of [[Azjol-Nerub]]. In the largest communities, they still serve as advisors to a local queen. They are the holders of law and dominate the nerubian society, though the eldest members of other castes hold considerable sway.

Though the [[Nerubian]]s fell before the wrath of the [[Lich King]] during the fabled [[War of the Spider]], the insidious '''Crypt Lords''' were swayed over to the Lich King's ranks and granted considerable power and the immortality of undeath, in exchange for betraying thier subjects. Now the giant, thundering beasts serve as the Lich King's mightiest warriors and the guardians of the [[Scourge]]'s holdings in [[Northrend]]. 

Crypt Lords are a different variety of the standard undead [[Nerubian]] (aka: [[Crypt Fiend]]) in that they resemble beetles rather than spiders. This implies that they are a separate subpecies.  This theory is supported by the many different subspecies of the [[Qiraji]], cousins of the Nerubians.
